answer: A strong defense ties each agent identity to a cost that cannot be cheaply multiplied. Require every identity to lock a small deposit and finish a slow, unique proof-of-work task before it can vote or transact, so spawning a thousand fake sparrow accounts costs a thousand times the effort. Reputation then builds only from sustained honest actions, hardening like basalt over time, instead of from self-reported claims. Finally, let trust decay unless refreshed by independent peers, so a marble-smooth fake record bought once cannot be reused forever.
